column1: # harness: python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli -q -p no:randomly -p no:cacheprovider
#          detached-equivalent worktree with no .venv of its own. pyproject
#          addopts supply -m 'not integration and not stress' --timeout=30
# ** THE INTERPRETER IS PART OF THE HARNESS, NOT A DETAIL. Run this sweep with
#    an interpreter that is (a) NOT the Microsoft-Store MSIX python and (b)
#    by absolute path. Do NOT rely on bare `python`: on this box that resolves
#    to the Store alias, which is neither, and it moves 10 rows on its own.
#    See "WHAT DISCRIMINATES" below for the measurement. **
# ** THE `Git-Bash` IN THE HARNESS LINE ABOVE IS WRONG for the run that
#    produced the 226-row core, and is left in place only as the record of
#    what was written. Measured 2026-09-08: under Git-Bash,
#    test_valid_bash_syntax PASSED on both interpreters -- so the run that
#    recorded it as a FAILURE cannot have been launched from Git-Bash. It was
#    a PowerShell (WSL bash) launch. This mattered for exactly the two rows
#    now fixed, and after that fix the launcher no longer moves any row --
#    which is the point of the fix. Recording the launcher is still worth
#    doing; recording it wrongly is how a harness note becomes a trap. **
# STABLE CORE: 224 failures across 57 files. DIFF AGAINST THIS.
#   0xC0000142. Worktree clean and HEAD unmoved across the run; no other
#   python.exe was running pytest or run_tests_parallel.py at launch.
#   Nodeids taken from the `FAILED ` lines of a run redirected WHOLE to a file.
# DO NOT PIPE THE RUN THROUGH tail/head IF YOU INTEND TO DIFF THE FAILURE SET.
# The summary line is printed LAST and always survives a tail; the FAILED
# nodeids scroll off. A `| tail -25` capture of a sweep at this commit held the
# summary and only 24 of its 233 nodeids -- all 24 happened to be baseline
# rows, which reads as a clean "0 new" off a 10% sample. Redirect to a file.
# 227 -> 226 rows, 58 -> 59 files, measured at 162965ad21. Against the frozen
# 2026-08-18 core: 4 nodeids are NEW and 5 frozen rows now PASS.
#   NEW (all four reproduce standalone, so none is order pollution):
# This is drift accumulated since the 2026-08-18 freeze, not a recent
# regression: the frozen list went three weeks without a resweep, and the
# 2026-08-20 attempt at one was invalidated (321F/9071P/102S/9E with 253
# STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED caused by a concurrent heavyweight pytest).
# --- HARNESS SENSITIVITY: 13 ROWS -- NOW DIAGNOSED, SEE "WHAT DISCRIMINATES"
# A SECOND clean single-process run at this same commit, from a different
# session and a different working environment, reported
# also with zero errors and zero DLL-init failures. The two runs are NOT
# set-identical. As of the 2026-09-08 second amendment the cause of every one
# of these 13 is known and named below -- 2 are FIXED and gone from the list,
# 10 are the interpreter, 1 is the network. This section is kept as the record
# of what was observed; do not read it as "unexplained flakiness" any more.
#   Failed in the other run, PASS here (10). All ten also pass STANDALONE in
#   this worktree, i.e. they are artifacts of that run's environment:
#   Passed in the other run, FAIL here (3). These fail standalone here too, and
#   the first two are ALSO in the frozen 2026-08-18 core -- so on these rows the
#   run recorded in this file agrees with history and the other run is the
# The skip counts differ too (102 here vs 96 there), which is the shape of an
# environment difference rather than of flakiness.
# All 13 were run as a controlled experiment: SAME worktree, SAME cwd, SAME
# commit, varying one factor at a time. Two independent factors account for
# all of them. Neither is flakiness -- each is deterministic given its factor.
# FACTOR 1 -- WHICH `bash` IS FIRST ON PATH.  Affects 2 rows. NOW FIXED; both
# rows are GONE from the list below (226 -> 224 rows, 59 -> 57 files):
#   Both shelled out to `bash -n <windows path>`. A sweep launched from
#   Git-Bash finds C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\bash.exe (Cygwin, which reads a
#   `C:\...` argument) and PASSES; a sweep launched from PowerShell finds
#   C:\WINDOWS\system32\bash.exe (WSL, POSIX), which eats the backslashes and
#   returns rc=127 `/bin/bash: C:UsersdiegoAppData...: No such file or
#   directory`, so it FAILS. Same commit, opposite verdict, on launcher alone.
#   That is a portability bug in the TEST. Both now feed the script on stdin
#   (`bash -n -`), which removes the path from the picture; the fixture skips
#   with a reason when no usable bash is present. Verified green in all four
#   cells of {Git-Bash, PowerShell} x {Store python, repo .venv python}, and
#   `bash -n -` still returns rc=2 on genuinely broken shell under both bashes,
#   so the check keeps its teeth.
# FACTOR 2 -- WHICH INTERPRETER RUNS PYTEST.  Accounts for all 10 rows in the
# "Failed in the other run, PASS here" list above. Measured, same worktree and
#   Mechanism, two facets of the same factor:
#       Microsoft-Store MSIX app-execution alias, returning the real packaged
#       `python3.11.exe` under sys.base_prefix. The 9 argv-shape tests assert
#       against raw `sys.executable`, which under the Store alias is the
#       0-byte reparse point -- so product and test disagree by construction.
#       the same fact in a louder form: it does shutil.copy2(sys.executable,
#       ...) and dies with OSError [Errno 22] because you cannot read the alias.
#       the product inserts `--system`, which the test does not expect. The
#       Store alias is not in a venv; the repo .venv is.
#   These are NOT product regressions and NOT order pollution. They are the
#   reason the harness block above now pins the interpreter by absolute path.
# FACTOR 2 ALSO EXPLAINS THE SKIP DELTA in shape (102 vs 96): interpreter- and
# version-gated skips move with it. Not separately measured -- do not quote a
# number for that, only the direction.
# THE 13th ROW IS NEITHER FACTOR -- IT IS THE NETWORK. It stays in the list:
#   The test patches `hermes_cli.banner.subprocess.run`, but the ls-remote it
#   means to intercept is issued by `_check_via_rev` through
#   patch is inert and a REAL `git ls-remote https://github.com/NousResearch/
#   hermes-agent.git` goes out over the network on every run. It passes when
#   that call succeeds within its 10s timeout and fails otherwise. Measured
#   timeout fired, run_text_capture killed the tree (`taskkill /PID .. /T /F`
#   is visible in the call log), _check_via_rev returned None, and the test's
#   `assert result == 1` failed. So this row flips on transient upstream
#   availability, under BOTH interpreters and BOTH launchers.
#   NOT FIXED -- out of scope for the 2026-09-08 second amendment, which was
#   scoped to the two bash rows. It is a real test defect (unmocked network in
#   a unit suite, plus up to ~60s of wall clock) and is the obvious next fix:
#   patch run_text_capture at `hermes_cli.banner`'s import site, or at
# Removed exactly the two FACTOR 1 rows, after fixing the tests, and CONFIRMED
# BY A FRESH FULL SINGLE-PROCESS SWEEP at the fix commit:
#   No other pytest process on the box at launch (checked, and the sweep was
#   deferred ~10 min until three concurrent ones had drained -- launching into
#   those is what invalidated the 2026-08-20 attempt). Output redirected WHOLE
#   to a file and set-diffed; never piped through tail/head.
#   Git-Bash, in a worktree with no .venv of its own.
# Set-diff of that sweep against the 224 rows below: ZERO rows missing, ONE
# extra. Both bash rows are confirmed absent from the failure set by full
# sweep, not merely by targeted rerun. Also note the skip count came back at
# 102, matching the 226-row core -- consistent with FACTOR 2, since both runs
# When set-diffing a `-q` sweep, STRIP THE ` - <message>` SUFFIX from each
# `FAILED ` line before comparing. pytest -q appends a truncated failure
# message to the nodeid; comparing raw lines reports every one of those rows
# as simultaneously added and removed. A first pass here did exactly that and
# read as 4 added / 3 removed against a true delta of 1 added / 0 removed.
#   THE ONE EXTRA ROW -- NOT ADDED TO THE CORE, deliberately:
#   It PASSES STANDALONE (4 passed) and passes when run alongside both files
#   touched by this amendment, so it is an in-sweep ORDER-POLLUTION artifact,
#   not a product failure and not attributable to the fix -- the conftest
#   change is purely additive (one session-scoped fixture, instantiated only by
#   the two tests above), so it cannot move another row. It is left OUT of the
#   frozen core for the same reason the 2026-08-20 amendment removed 19 such
#   rows: a baseline of pollution victims is not a tripwire. Recorded here so
#   the next sweep does not open a bug when it appears -- expect it to come and
#   go. If it ever fails STANDALONE, that is a real regression; check that
#   first before treating it as this artifact.
# WHOEVER RUNS THE NEXT FULL SWEEP: expect 224 core rows, plus or minus that
# one pollution row. If you get 226 with the two bash rows back, you are on a
# commit before this amendment, not looking at a regression.
# THIS IS A BASELINE, NOT A REGRESSION LIST. The largest families are platform
# failures (POSIX-only APIs on Windows), not defects from any recent change:
# Why this file can exist at all: pytest-timeout's `thread` method -- the only
# one available on Windows -- answered a cap breach with os._exit(1), so a
# single slow test ended the process with no summary line and a failure set
# that depended on where it died. tests/_nonfatal_timeout.py makes a breach
# fail one test instead, which is what makes a frozen list meaningful.
# --- PRIOR FREEZE HISTORY (superseded by the 2026-09-08 amendment above) -----
# 9 independent full runs, every one printing a summary line and
# FDGUARD-SUMMARY collected=9434 CLEAN. The core was set-identical (not merely
# count-identical) in 5 of them: V1, V3, W1, X2, X3.
#   A   249 failed, 9086 passed, 102 skipped, 12 warnings in 2803.39s (0:46:43)
#   V1  248 failed, 9087 passed, 102 skipped, 12 warnings in 3139.93s (0:52:19)
#   V2  249 failed, 9086 passed, 102 skipped, 12 warnings in 2482.19s (0:41:22)
#   V3  248 failed, 9087 passed, 102 skipped, 12 warnings in 3128.04s (0:52:08)
#   W1  248 failed, 9087 passed, 102 skipped, 12 warnings in 2795.43s (0:46:35)
#   W2  249 failed, 9086 passed, 102 skipped, 12 warnings in 2808.31s (0:46:48)
#   X1  249 failed, 9086 passed, 102 skipped, 12 warnings in 1806.28s (0:30:06)
#   X2  248 failed, 9087 passed, 102 skipped, 12 warnings in 1713.45s (0:28:33)
#   X3  248 failed, 9087 passed, 102 skipped, 12 warnings in 2838.29s (0:47:18)
# The remaining runs were core + exactly ONE rotating timing-sensitive test.
# All four such tests were identified and fixed; none is part of the core:
#     FIXED: holder hold-budget + spawn budget scaled
#     FIXED: READY handshake before write (was a race, not a deadline)
# AMENDED 2026-08-20 (0a5e268a96): 248 -> 246 across 60 files. Removed the two
# test_kanban_reclaim_claim_lock_guard.py rows. They were never product
# failures -- the 2026-08-17 isolation triage classified both POLLUTION. The
# tests spawned the POSIX binaries `true` and `sleep`, which on Windows resolve
# only via Git/MSYS usr/bin, so any earlier test that narrowed PATH made them
# raise FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2]. They now spawn sys.executable and take
# no PATH lookup, so they pass in-sweep.
# single-process resweep removed 19 rows: all 16 test_gui_command.py failures
# and all 3 test_dashboard_auth_password_login.py failures. These were
# order-pollution victims, not product regressions. The app-state leak fix at
# 73bab4a7c7 and the sys.modules restoration at c42235e8a1 landed after the
# db0977b4c0 freeze. Evidence: detached worktree pinned at c0008fb8ad,
